Progress Log

Newest entries first. Every implementation slice adds an entry. Append-only: never delete, never reorder, never edit a previous entry.

Each slice is an <article data-slice="..." data-date="YYYY-MM-DD"> with the following <dl> entries: Branch, PR, Changed, Verification, Assumptions, GDD coverage, Followups.

How to add a slice entry

Copy this template, fill in the values, and insert it as the new top entry under <main id="entries">.

<article data-slice="short-title" data-date="YYYY-MM-DD">
  <h3>Short Title</h3>
  <dl>
    <dt>Branch</dt><dd><code>feature/short-name</code></dd>
    <dt>PR</dt><dd>#N (when known)</dd>
    <dt>Changed</dt><dd>one paragraph naming the user-facing change and the key files / helpers / defaults that landed.</dd>
    <dt>Verification</dt><dd>dash checks, type-check, relevant unit tests, build, smoke (where applicable). Note any known-tolerated lint warnings or skipped checks.</dd>
    <dt>Assumptions</dt><dd>assumptions made under a Recommended default. One sentence per assumption.</dd>
    <dt>GDD coverage</dt><dd>which rows in <code>docs/GDD_COVERAGE.json</code> flipped to <code>partial</code> or <code>done</code>, or which <code>docs/gdd/*.html</code> files gained a Build log entry.</dd>
    <dt>Followups</dt><dd>any new <code>F-NNN</code> entries created. Link to them.</dd>
  </dl>
</article>

Pre-compile mine materials at load to kill the first-use shader-compile stall

Branch
claude/instanced-grid-rewrite-es0i83 (follow-on to the decoration-sharing slices below).
PR
Pending.
Changed
Diagnosed from the preview-build real-device telemetry (GET /api/performance/insights?device=real). The instancing and decoration-sharing slices resolved the F-074 GC-pause class: on the newest builds (0.1.203.272496/272515) steady state is a locked ~60 fps, the heap no longer sawtooths, and the old 4.5 s freeze (build 269524, worst p95 4475 ms) is gone (worst p95 16.8 ms). What remained was intermittent ~0.6 to 1.0 s stalls, every one LoAF-attributed to FrameRequestCallback, with the same stalls present on a desktop Apple M-series WebGPU session (766 ms frame, 4004 ms long-frame window) where GC and reconcile are not credible causes. That signature is first-use shader/pipeline compilation: three compiles each material program lazily on its first draw, so a new tint/kind appearing mid-play (a stratum tint, an ore crystal, a rock tier, a shard glow, the darkness overlay) hitches a frame. This slice pre-compiles every mine material once at mine load so the cost is paid behind the load, not per action: a new warmMineMaterials in mine-canvas.tsx builds one tiny offscreen mesh per material and calls renderer.compileAsync in a mount effect. The instanced block bodies (dirt, ore, rock, metal) warm on an InstancedMesh because the instanced draw compiles a distinct program; crystals, tunnel floor, gas, boulder, shards, supports, and the darkness buckets warm on plain meshes. The variant enumeration lives in the new mine-material-warmup.ts (block node materials) plus the shard/support/darkness sets the canvas already owns; the palette now exports its dirt and rock tint arrays for it. Best-effort: if the renderer lacks compileAsync or it throws, materials fall back to lazy compile (today's behavior), so the warm-up can never break the mine. No version bump; MINE_VERSION stays at 50; SIM_VERSION stays at 4.
Verification
Partial in the authoring container (the egress-blocked @randroids-dojo/vibekit dependency prevents tsc/vitest/build/Playwright locally). Ran: Biome clean on all changed files; em-dash and git diff --check clean. Manual review confirmed the warm-up compiles the same programs the game draws (same geometry attribute set, and the instanced program is warmed on an InstancedMesh) and that the shard glow set matches FallingRockShard's discrete glows. This one needs on-device confirmation: after deploy, the newest build's session drilldown should show maxFrameMs and per-session stallCount drop toward the steady-state 16.8 ms, and the desktop long-frame windows shrink. CI runs the full gate.
Assumptions
Recommended default: warm on compileAsync in a post-mount useEffect (not layout) so the first paint is not blocked; the compile burst lands just after mount, behind the mine's load. Warm only the live detail tier (the other tier compiles if the player flips quality, which re-runs the effect). Scoped to the mine render materials; the surface-village and workshop/holodeck materials are out of scope. If telemetry still shows a residual stall, the next suspect is the sim-side tickFalls all-cells scan. Rule 13: mine tips reviewed, no change (render-path perf, no player rule changed). Rule 14: stamp review done, none added.
GDD coverage
No status changes. Build-log entry added to docs/gdd/06-mining.html.
Followups
Appended a progress note to F-075. If a stall survives the warm-up on real hardware, profile the tickFalls scan (it iterates every world cell per fall) as the remaining candidate.

Share the tunnel-floor and darkness-overlay geometry and materials (surface-drop and crush lag)

Branch
claude/instanced-grid-rewrite-es0i83 (follow-on to the support-sharing entry below).
PR
Pending.
Changed
User-reported lag when dropping several levels from the surface (fatal and non-fatal) and when crushed by a falling rock. Both are one action that opens the view window onto a batch of previously-unseen cells at once: a drop from the surface reveals the shaft and the dark region below it, and a crush jumps the window to the wreck. The solid bodies are instanced, but two per-cell overlays were still inline geometry/material JSX: the recessed tunnel floor on every carved (empty) cell, and the darkness plane on every cell past the lamp. So the reveal built a geometry, a material, and, for the floor, a Color per cell in that single tick, an allocation burst that reads as the F-074 GC-pause lag. Applied the shipped sharing pattern: one shared box geometry and a per-biome jittered node material (tunnelFloorMaterial in mine-block-materials.ts, tint jitter in the shader like the block bodies) for the floor; one shared plane geometry and an opacity-bucketed MeshBasicMaterial cache for the darkness plane (opacity is discrete: it only shows at max zoom over a narrow ramp). Both meshes now carry dispose={null} and create nothing on mount. Visuals are effectively identical (the floor keeps a stable per-cell tint jitter; darkness buckets to 0.02 opacity, below perception). No version bump; MINE_VERSION stays at 50; SIM_VERSION stays at 4.
Verification
Partial in the authoring container (same egress-blocked @randroids-dojo/vibekit dependency prevents tsc/vitest/build/Playwright locally). Ran: Biome clean; em-dash and git diff --check clean. Manual review confirmed the shared tunnel material reproduces the recessed floor and the bucketed darkness matches the ramped overlay. CI runs the full gate; real-device confirmation via the per-build telemetry A/B after deploy.
Assumptions
Recommended default: move the tunnel-floor tint jitter into the shared node material's shader (matching how the block bodies dropped per-cell variedColor Color allocation) rather than keep a per-cell material, and bucket darkness opacity rather than mint a material per exact value. Considered and skipped this pass: memoizing SurfaceSkin (it renders every tick and allocates a Color per column) is unsafe without a portal signature, because a portal activated mid-trip mutates the mine in place and a mine-identity memo would leave its glow stale; noted as a follow-on that needs the signature. If a multi-second freeze persists after this, the remaining suspects are JS-heap GC pressure and the sim-side tickFalls all-cells scan, both of which need device telemetry to confirm. Rule 13: mine tips reviewed, no change. Rule 14: stamp review done, none added.

No status changes. Build-log entry added to docs/gdd/06-mining.html.
Followups
Memoizing or gating SurfaceSkin (with a portal signature) to stop its per-tick Color allocation, and profiling the tickFalls scan, are candidates under the F-075 follow-through if telemetry still shows fall-time stalls.

Imperative instanced block grid: stop the scroll-churn behind the fall and ladder lag (F-075 escalation)

Branch
claude/instanced-grid-rewrite-es0i83.
PR
Pending.
Changed
The user still reports lag when falling, walking down ladders, and at random, after the F-075 cell-signature cache, the DPR cap, and the geometry-sharing leak fix. The cell cache only helps cells that stay on screen; every action that scrolls the window (a step down, and especially a multi-row fall) still mounted a fresh row of block meshes and unmounted the row that left, so React reconciled a scene-graph mount/unmount burst per action, which is the residual churn F-075 named the imperative-instanced-grid escalation for. Shipped that escalation. The static solid bodies (dirt, ore body, non-fallen rock, metal), the dominant on-screen mass, now stream through an imperative InstancedMesh grid instead of one React-reconciled mesh per cell: new src/components/mine-instanced-grid.ts (InstancedBlockGrid, one InstancedMesh per (geometry, shared material) bucket, two-pass matrix streaming with lazy pool creation and doubling growth), new three-free planning core src/components/mine-block-plan.ts (the pooled BlockInstancePlan and the instancedBlockDraw classifier, node-testable), and instancedBlockBody in mine-block-render.tsx as the single source mapping a cell to its geometry/material/rotation (mirrors MineBlockBody exactly). In mine-canvas.tsx the render loop fills the plan for every instanced cell (on cache hit and miss alike, since the plan is not cached) and a layout effect rewrites the instance matrices and counts after each render, off the frame path; buildCellEntry now skips the body for those cells (ore keeps its crystals as a React overlay). Scrolling the window rewrites matrices and counts only, mounting and unmounting nothing. Materials are the existing uniform-tinted singletons and the per-cell tint jitter already rides positionWorld (which includes the instance transform), so the blocks render pixel-identical. Teetering and fallen blocks, boulders, magma, gas, part-caches, tunnels, ladders, planks, beacons, drops, bags, cracks, darkness overlays, and the dynamite charge all stay on the React path (sparse, and the teeter wobble needs per-block transforms). No version bump, no SIM_VERSION/MINE_VERSION change (render-only).
Verification

Ran instead: Biome (biome ci . via pnpm dlx, syntactic so it needs no deps) clean on all changed files and the repo (one pre-existing broken-symlink warning only); the em-dash check and git diff --check clean. Added src/components/mine-block-plan.test.ts covering the instancedBlockDraw contract (which kinds instance; teetering/fallen/inline-material/empty stay React) and the pooled-plan reuse and rotation-flag logic; it imports no runtime three so it runs in the node vitest env. The required CI gate (typecheck, unit, build, Playwright smoke) runs the parts this container could not. Manual review confirmed the instance transforms match the React block transforms (translate for dirt/ore/metal, translate plus the same cellHash rotation for rock) and that dispose={null} geometry/material singletons are never disposed by the grid. Real-device verdict comes from the per-build telemetry A/B after deploy (heap span and stall counts on ?device=real).
Assumptions
Recommended default: bucket by the existing shared uniform-tinted material rather than switch the block materials to per-instance color, because bucketing needs no shader change and stays pixel-identical (a handful of buckets per view: a few strata/biome dirt tints, one rock tint, metal), where per-instance color would have rippled into the Holodeck consumer and been unverifiable without a real GPU. Scoped to the static solid bodies (the mass that dominates the cell count and the scroll churn); darkness overlays and tunnel floors are still React and are the next lever if telemetry shows residual scroll churn (darkness needs per-instance opacity buckets, tunnel floors a shared jitter material). No per-frame work added: the grid updates at input cadence in a layout effect, and its apply() plus the pooled plan reuse module scratch so steady state allocates nothing (frame-loop rule respected; a new InstancedMesh is built only when a new material bucket first appears). Share mine block geometries to stop the per-cell GPU buffer leak (phone freeze fix)

Branch
claude/performance-analyzer-telemetry-jtb43n (restarted from main).
PR
Pending.
Changed
The real cause of the user's multi-second phone freezes, found after the F-075 cache and the DPR cap only dented them. Real-device telemetry showed the heap trough rising across a session (about 7 MB to 77 MB), a retention leak rather than churn. Root cause: MineBlockBody attaches shared singleton materials with dispose={null} (never dispose a shared material), which also stops R3F from disposing the mesh's per-cell geometry on unmount, so every cell that changed signature or fell out of the F-075 element cache leaked its GPU buffer. The dominant dirt/rock/ore/metal/gas/boulder bodies now draw from four shared geometry singletons in the new src/components/mine-block-geometries.ts (a rounded 0.94 cube reproducing drei's RoundedBox extrude exactly, a tighter metal cube, the rock dodecahedron, the boulder icosahedron); per-cell rotation and material stay on the mesh, only the geometry is shared. With the geometry a module constant, dispose={null} is now correct and nothing leaks. Version 0.1.203 with a player-facing note; MINE_VERSION and SIM_VERSION unchanged.
Verification
Passed: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit; pnpm test (992); Biome; pnpm build; dash and git diff --check; Playwright mine-core, mine-viewport, release-notifications (31 passed, includes the fatal-fall, crush-camera, and gated-rock render specs). Visual proof: a scripted dig screenshot shows dirt as the same beveled rounded cubes (correct edge highlights, no broken normals) and boulders as clean faceted icosahedra, identical to before. Leak proof: with perf telemetry on and its geometries count intercepted from the trace POST, a 55-action dig session holds a flat live geometry count (122, 122, 132) instead of climbing with the cells dug, i.e. the count is now bounded by the visible window, not accumulating.
Assumptions
Recommended default: reproduce drei's rounded-box extrude (createShape + toCreasedNormals at 0.4 rad, imported from three/examples/jsm as the project already does for bloom and RoomEnvironment) so the blocks stay pixel-identical, verified by screenshot. Scoped to the six block bodies (the meshes that both dominate the cell count and carry dispose={null}); overlay meshes that do not set dispose={null} already dispose normally. Rule 13: mine tips reviewed for 0.1.203, no change (no mine mechanic, economy, control, hazard, shop, or recovery rule changed). Rule 14: stamp review done, none added (a leak fix is not stamp material).
GDD coverage
No status changes. Build-log entry added to docs/gdd/06-mining.html.

Closes the remaining phone-lag thread tracked under the F-074/F-075 follow-through. Prevention captured: the dispose={null} geometry-leak trap is now documented in .claude/rules/frame-loop-performance.md (shared material plus per-cell geometry equals a GPU-buffer leak; share the geometry too).

Cap the low-tier mine canvas at DPR 1.5 (phone lag follow-up)

Branch
claude/performance-analyzer-telemetry-jtb43n (same 0.1.202 slice as the guest-clerk-scope entry below; one PR).
PR
Pending (folded into the 0.1.202 PR).
Changed
User still reports "a ton of lag" on the phone after the F-075 cell cache shipped (build 269749). Fresh real-device telemetry (session 6d25c6) confirms it: steady state is fine (avg 23 ms) but multi-second FrameRequestCallback stalls persist with a 7 to 122 MB heap sawtooth. Local SwiftShader cannot reproduce the sawtooth (a fall-and-dig-heavy 50 s profile on this branch samples 1.8 MB total, heap 31 to 47 MB), so the dominant cost is not app-JS allocation; the top allocators are all three.js renderer internals (getForRender, createBindings, createAttribute) scaling with the roughly 180 draw calls the phone reports, plus pixel fill at DPR 2.25. This slice takes the highest-confidence, lowest-risk lever: GraphicsFeatures gained a maxDpr (low tier 1.5, high tier 2) and the mine Canvas uses dpr={[1, features.maxDpr]} instead of a hardcoded [1, 2]. The phone's webgl2-forced low-tier path now renders a 448-wide CSS canvas into a 672 px buffer instead of 896 px, about 44 percent fewer pixels shaded per frame, which cuts steady frame time and thermal throttling (throttling amplifies the GC stalls on a low battery). Verified locally: with the low tier pinned and a touch context, the effective DPR dropped from 2.0 to exactly 1.5; the high tier is unchanged.
Verification
Passed: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit; pnpm test (graphics-quality gains a maxDpr assertion; release-note fixtures updated for the added phone-resolution line); Biome; pnpm build; dash and git diff --check. Instrumented Playwright at the phone viewport (448x923, DPR 2.25) confirmed the low-tier buffer width is 672 px (effective DPR 1.5) and the webgl2-forced renderer, matching the phone. Real verdict via the per-build telemetry A/B once a phone session lands on 0.1.202.
Assumptions
Recommended default: 1.5 over a more aggressive 1.25, keeping legibility on a small screen while still roughly halving fill. This is one lever, not the whole fix; the remaining multi-second stalls are most likely GC of the large heap and/or first-use shader compiles, tracked for the next slice against fresh 0.1.202 telemetry (candidate deeper fix: an imperative instanced cell grid to collapse the roughly 180 draw calls, the documented F-075 escalation). Rule 13: mine tips reviewed for 0.1.202, no change (internal resolution is not a mine rule). Rule 14: stamp review done, none added.
GDD coverage
No status changes. Build-log entry added to docs/gdd/06-mining.html.
Followups

The mine canvas rebuilt every visible cell's JSX on every store tick, so React reconciled the whole grid per action and per fall row. Cells now build through a per-cell signature cache: the cell-field fingerprint (cellRenderSignature) lives beside MineBlockBody in mine-block-render.tsx so the enumeration sits with the JSX that reads the fields, and the canvas appends its view-layer inputs (quantized darkness opacity and damage, dynamite preview, salvage and selection state, handler presence). On a signature match the tick hands React the previous element references and reconciliation bails out on the whole cell subtree; the mine world mutates in place, so object identity could never stand in for this. Click handlers dispatch through a ref (cached elements never hold a stale prop), the teeter mount ref is a stable callback with wobble targets refreshed per render, the builder sits at module scope so cached closures cannot pin the render scope that built them, and eviction sweeps cells that left the window by render generation instead of dumping the live set. Also fixed the heap-churn probe: headless Chrome freezes performance.memory without --enable-precise-memory-info, so the probe measured nothing silently; it now passes the flag and warns on a flat heap.
Verification
Passed: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit; pnpm test (995); Biome on touched files; pnpm build; dash and git diff --check; Playwright mine-core, mine-ui, mine-viewport, mine-navigation (36 passed) before the review pass and re-run after it. Measurement: CDP sampling heap profile over identical 40 s scripted play drops total sampled allocation 5.8 MB to 2.7 MB and removes the react-reconciler stacks from the top allocation sites; the 75 s heap-churn probe reads parity within world-seed noise on desktop-class headless (2.51 baseline vs 2.68 MB/s), so the real verdict is the per-build telemetry A/B (/api/performance/insights?device=real, byBuild) once a phone session lands on this build. Review pass applied four findings: builder to module scope, derived bookkeeping out of the cache entry (also fixing a gas-wisp double count on cache misses), the cell fingerprint moved beside the shared body, generation-sweep eviction.
Assumptions
Recommended default: signature cache over React.memo (cells fan into six z-ordered bucket arrays, and in-place world mutation defeats prop identity) and over an imperative instanced grid (documented endgame if telemetry still shows reconcile churn; nothing here is wasted on that path, the signature becomes its dirty check). Sub-0.001 quantization of darkness opacity and damage in the signature trades invisible drift for not rebuilding every darkened cell during zoom eases. Rule 13: tips reviewed, no change (no player-facing rule changed; no version bump for an internal render fix). Rule 14: stamp review done, none added (bug-fix class work is explicitly not stamp material).

Added a safe account-route error normalizer so the dialog now surfaces whitelisted route errors such as guest save not found or same-origin request required for the next live click. After the fourth manual pass showed same-origin request required, account mutation requests now carry x-vibebots-account-mutation: 1, and the mutation guard accepts that app-owned header as the embedded-browser fallback while still rejecting ordinary cross-site posts. After the fifth manual pass showed return-to-window and save-click friction, the handoff callback now retries while the Clerk development session settles, the callback query is removed once status resolves into a signed-in, cloud-loaded, or conflict state, and loadAccountStatus automatically claims a signed-in device save when no cloud save exists. The design recommends Clerk through Vercel Marketplace for the first VibeBots implementation, keeps the player row as the save authority, handles existing-cloud-save conflicts without destructive automatic merges, accounts for partitioned iframe cookies, and defines a provider-neutral account-linking boundary for later VibeKit extraction. The account API boundary now adds /api/account/status, /api/account/claim, /api/account/load, and /api/account/handoff/*, plus an account resolver boundary that normalizes provider output before routes use it and will call the Clerk resolver once the dependency is approved. The mine settings menu now has an Account dialog backed by client parsers and store actions for account status, saving the current signed-in run, explicitly loading the existing cloud save in conflict state, starting the one-time handoff, and finishing the handoff from accountHandoff query params. The sign-in button remains disabled in the current env until the public Clerk sign-in URL exists, and the real signed-in resolver still needs Clerk package/setup approval. Redirect URL construction is now a covered pure helper so Clerk's return parameter preserves the one-time handoff token. The reusable claim coordinator now lives in src/server/account-link-core.ts behind AccountLinkStore, while src/server/account-linking.ts is the VibeBots Clerk-column adapter. Embedded sign-in handoff now has a database-backed, short-lived token flow: start stores the current guest player and sanitized return path; finish consumes the token after sign-in, claims the stored row, switches the active save-slot cookie, or returns a non-destructive conflict. Added .env.example and README env docs for the future Clerk keys without committing secrets. Files: .env.example, README.md, docs/research/account-sync-google-signin.html, docs/gdd/10-account-sync.html, docs/gdd/index.html, docs/GDD_COVERAGE.json, docs/FOLLOWUPS.html, src/server/account-handoff.ts, src/server/account-handoff.test.ts, src/server/account-link-core.ts, src/server/account-link-core.test.ts, src/server/account-linking.ts, src/server/account-linking.test.ts, src/server/account-session.ts, src/server/account-session.test.ts, src/server/account-summary.ts, src/app/api/account/status/route.ts, src/app/api/account/claim/route.ts, src/app/api/account/load/route.ts, src/app/api/account/handoff/start/route.ts, src/app/api/account/handoff/finish/route.ts, src/app/api/account/account-routes.test.ts, src/app/api/account/handoff-routes.test.ts, src/components/mine-account-popup.tsx, src/components/mine-account-popup.test.ts, src/components/mine-panel.tsx, src/state/mine-api-client.ts, src/state/mine-api-client.test.ts, src/state/mine-store.ts, src/state/mine-store.test.ts, src/server/player.ts, src/server/player.test.ts, src/server/db.ts, src/server/db.test.ts.

Menu lift: the bot rises above an open sheet (slice O)

Branch
workshop-o-lift, from origin/main. Verified on a temporary CI branch, then fast-forwarded to main.
PR
None (direct main). Direct response to follow-up feedback after trying slice N: "we definitely need to move the bot and displayed part higher when larger menus are open."
Changed
When a tall menu sheet is open (Tune/Garage/Shop), the bot now lifts up into the band between the top header and the sheet, instead of hiding behind the sheet. Implemented as a camera view offset, not a camera move: a new MenuLift component in src/components/workshop-canvas.tsx calls camera.setViewOffset to shift the rendered image upward by a fraction of the viewport. Because the offset lives in the projection matrix, raycasting (drag targeting) stays consistent with what is drawn. src/components/workshop-panel.tsx computes the lift from the open sheet's measured content height (taller menu covers more, so it lifts more), centering the bot in the band between the header and the sheet top, and passes it as the menuLift prop. The lift is forced to zero on the Build tab and whenever the sheet is collapsed, so the hero-drag band and its pinned screen coordinates never move. The applied lift is published on the canvas dataset.menuLift for tests. UI-only: no SIM_VERSION/MINE_VERSION change. Package version 0.1.196.

The scripted 390x760 probe (scripts/playtest-sheet.mjs) now asserts the lift too: Build lift is exactly 0 and the Garage lift is 0.165 (>0.05), with zero console errors. Before/after captures reviewed by eye confirm the visible pixels move: the bot goes from mostly behind the Garage sheet to fully framed above it, clear of the header (Rule 10, pixel movement confirmed visually; a WebGL framebuffer read is not reliable across the WebGPU fallback, so the automated guard is the projection param that feeds setViewOffset). New e2e "the bot lifts above an open menu sheet (O)" asserts dataset.menuLift is 0 on Build/collapsed and >0.05 on Garage. Full 17-test workshop.spec.ts green (the drag tests still pass because they drag with the sheet collapsed, lift 0). Assumptions
The lift is capped at 0.22 of the viewport and only applies on the menu tabs, because those are the "larger menus" the feedback named and the Build hero/carousel are canvas overlays whose screen anchors must stay fixed. A view offset was chosen over a camera move so drag raycasting stays correct and the fixed-camera drag e2e keep their pinned coordinates. Workshop remove cascades to the subtree, refund verified (user feedback, slice F of 5)

Branch
Verified on a temporary CI branch, then fast-forwarded to main.
PR
None (direct main). Feedback: removing a part in a stack should also remove everything attached after it, and refunds on remove/undo should be double-checked.
Changed
removeSelected no longer refuses parts with children; it removes the selected part plus its whole subtree via a new pure subtreeIids(design, rootIid) helper (BFS over parent-to-child connections), dropping every removed part and any connection touching one. The core is still never removable. The panel's selectedRemovable gate dropped its "no children" clause too (it was disabling the Remove button for any mid-stack part, which would have blocked the cascade in the UI), and the Remove button title now reads "Remove this part and anything attached to it". Refund audit: the workshop never mutates server inventory on place; owned counts come from a GET /api/shop and the available count is owned - designPartCounts(design), enforced server-side only at match-resolve. So removing parts (and undo restoring them) refunds automatically by recomputing the used count, no refund call needed. No sim, schema, SIM_VERSION, or MINE_VERSION change. Package version 0.1.187.
Verification
Dash check, git diff --check, tsc, Biome, full unit suite. New store tests: subtreeIids collects a part plus its descendants (and just itself for a leaf, everything for the core); removing a spin-mount with a saw blade on it drops both parts, designPartCounts shows both refunded, and undo restores both parts and their used counts. The Remove button (now enabled for any non-core part) drives removeSelected. pnpm build.
Assumptions
Refund is derived, not transactional (Rule 7: one consistent rule). Because the client never eagerly spends server inventory, there is nothing to "give back" on remove; the used count simply drops. If a future slice makes placement spend server inventory eagerly, this note flags where the explicit refund would go. Rule 13: mine tips reviewed, no change (workshop surface). Held-Input Cadence Survives Timer Jitter

Changed
Product fix in src/components/mine-input-cadence.ts: the held-input repeat chain died silently when a repeat timer fired a hair before its due time (the time guard rejected the attempt and the chain never rescheduled), which is why held digs stalled partway on loaded devices and CI runners. The chain now reschedules through a missed window with guaranteed forward progress (minimum 1ms delay), while a rejected action still ends the chain because cancel() clears the held input. Covered by a jittery-clock regression test whose first draft hot-looped by firing zero-delay timers with no time progress; both the product and the synthetic clock now guarantee progress. Test-side: the crush test drops a redundant post-activation camera poll that raced the playback's end, and the raid XP retry window widens to the same stall allowance as its siblings. No version bumps (input reliability fix; MINE_VERSION 48, SIM_VERSION 3, package 0.1.153 unchanged).

#80. Self-review (8-angle) and CodeRabbit converged on the same post-open findings: stale impact keys across trip resets, wreck cleanup below the ok-gate, a fixed ceiling too short for long falls, and digTo hold overshoot; all closed in the review-fix commit on the branch.
Changed
Fixed the five tests that kept the scheduled Full E2E matrix red on main (every scheduled run in visible history was failing; the required parallel gate stayed green). Two product changes: the fatal-fall and falling-rock-crush trip report is now gated on the rendered impact frame instead of a wall-clock timer, so frame-starved devices no longer see the report before the crash lands (canvas marks the impact via a new fallVisualImpactKey in src/state/mine-store.ts, JuiceOverlays waits for it with a 4s safety ceiling), and the Mine status HUD exposes data-scene-ready so tests can wait for the input gate that silently drops movement keys during load. Test-side: digTo holds the key for the bulk of a descent and finishes with paced presses (dirt takes 4 swings per row at pickaxe 1; the old 190ms press loop dropped 2 of 3 presses against the 620ms action cadence and blew the 60s budget on CI), walkUntilBaseIndicator is hold-based, walkToStallPrompt paces at the cadence, the held-cadence burst test asserts "four synchronous taps yield exactly one step" instead of racing the previous repeat window, the stratum banner test proves the one-shot 2.6s animation animates while alive instead of racing its lifetime, the crush test waits for camera settle before triggering and asserts report-after-impact ordering, and the raid XP pickup test waits for camera framing, mirrors the collected state in the /api/bunker mock after the second collect (a background refetch could revert the pickup), and extends pixel-poll timeouts. Fix No-Claim-On-File When Embedded In A Cross-Site Iframe

Branch
fix/embedded-iframe-claim-cookie
PR
#67
Changed
selling at the Assay Office while the game ran embedded in VibeCoded.games (an iframe loading vibe-bots.vercel.app under a different top-level site) failed with "no claim on file" (user-reported). Root cause: the vb_player identity cookie was SameSite=Lax, which browsers exclude from every request whose frame ancestry is cross-site, including the iframe's own same-origin fetches. With no cookie, getOrCreatePlayerId minted a fresh player on each call, so the cash-out POST ran as a new player with no mine_worlds row. The cookie is now SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned (CHIPS), so it flows in the embedded context, partitioned per top-level site, which browsers that block unpartitioned third-party cookies still accept. File: src/server/player.ts.
Verification
dash check, git diff --check, tsc --noEmit, biome check on the changed file. The fix is a cookie attribute change verified by reasoning against the SameSite and CHIPS specs; behavioral proof needs an HTTPS preview embedded cross-site (a Secure cookie will not set over http://localhost).
Assumptions
identity is partitioned per embedding host: a guest playing standalone and the same guest playing embedded get separate claims, which is consistent with guest-first identity (F-003) and unavoidable given modern browser storage partitioning.
GDD coverage
no coverage rows flipped; added a Build log entry to docs/gdd/06-mining.html (persistent claim, REQ-026).
Followups
none.

The cell's wobbling boolean became a fallIn countdown, resolveFalls/markWobbling became tickFalls/markUnstable, and the renderer trembles and warm-glows both rock and boulder harder as the countdown nears zero. Combat Legibility (fun-factor audit response)

Branch
feature/combat-legibility
PR
pending
Changed
response to the first VibeReview playtest (session docs/reviews/20260610-220517-4C845606), which found 60s exhibition matches ending with both bots at 100% hull. Root causes found by force probes: wheels (radius 0.4) protruded past the core face and ate every frontal contact below threshold; bots could not steer, so after the first clash they drifted onto parallel tracks and never re-engaged; the first impact burst was the only damage source (one-shot or nothing). Landed: weapon-first differential-drive steering (quaternion-rotated facing, cross-product steer, behind-hemisphere turns, all pure arithmetic), ram cycles (charge, back off, re-charge), damage restricted to bot-versus-bot contacts, weapon damage multiplier (x6), per-event damage cap (45) so the opening clash cannot one-shot, retuned threshold (20 N) and scale (0.22) from measured force distributions, wheel radius 0.34, core durability 180, SIM_VERSION 2. Second stock design (Brawler) because identical mirror bots always draw; the exhibition is now Brawler vs Rammer with design-name HUD labels, per-part damage pips, and timeout banners showing the deciding totals (epsilon-close totals are honest draws).
Verification
dash check, purity check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test (34; new stock-matchup test asserts the fight is destructive: Brawler loses over 20% of total durability and the Rammer wins), pnpm build, pnpm test:e2e. Tuning probes ran full 3600-tick matches against measured force distributions.
Assumptions
ground and self contacts deal no damage until arena hazards exist; per-event cap 45 trades guaranteed part destruction for multi-clash fights (F-007 stays open); steering gain 2, backoff 60 ticks at 0.8 speed.
GDD coverage
build-log entries on 02 (Brawler design, wheel sizing) and 03 (steering, ram cycles, damage model); REQ-001 strengthened in place (still partial).

F-008 and F-009 resolved; F-007 remains open with a progress note (part destruction not yet guaranteed per match).
